summary: MongoDB Atlas Admin API authentication on GCP uses OAuth 2.0 Service Accounts for API/administrative access, while cluster data access instead uses Workload Identity Federation (OIDC) for passwordless auth from GCP workloads.

facts.text: Atlas Admin API uses OAuth 2.0 Service Accounts with the Client Credentials flow; tokens are obtained from POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token and are valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds), reusable within that window.
Admin API authentication (managing projects, users, and networks) is a distinct concern from cluster data access (reading and writing documents) — the two use different auth mechanisms.

GCP does not provide a native Admin API integration; the recommended pattern is to store Atlas API credentials in GCP Secret Manager and retrieve them from the workload (Compute Engine, Cloud Run, GKE).
For cluster data access (not Admin API), Workload Identity Federation gives OIDC-based passwordless auth from a GCP Service Account to Atlas clusters on MongoDB 7.0.11+ running on M10+ tiers.

The MONGODB-OIDC connection string uses authMechanismProperties=ENVIRONMENT:gcp,TOKEN_RESOURCE:<audience>; supported by PyMongo 4.7+, Node.js driver 6.7+, Go driver 1.17+, and Java driver 5.1+, among other current drivers.
Assign minimal Atlas roles to service accounts — e.g. Project Data Access Admin — rather than Organization Owner.
IP-allowlist token usage to known CIDR blocks (CI/CD runners, GCP NAT ranges) and rotate secrets on a fixed cadence, roughly every 90 days.
Cache the 1-hour OAuth token and refresh it a few minutes before expiry rather than requesting a new token on every call.
Store credentials in GCP Secret Manager rather than plain environment variables.
No GCP-published SDK exists for the Atlas Admin API; implementations rely on generic OAuth 2.0 client libraries such as google-auth-library-python.
